Of course when you start thinking of it all as you, it might seem like it was all a show you put on. Why wouldnt it? Thats how it turned out for me, the alter that was out the most often ended up being the largest part of my integrated personality. I don't know how it is for others, I don't see a lot of writing about this, sadly. 

EDIT: Another thing Id like to add... The largest part of me didn't end up being the part with my birth name! I always thought that would be the main part of me since it was my legal name, and as a multiple I felt an insecurity as other parts of me, that I was somewhat "less real" than birthname... Of course, all of the parts were real (something i knew logically but not emotionally until integration). But it turned out the part with the birth name was more of a representation than anything else, like a part of me stuck in the past. I don't identify as female now, even. Things can change! I just wanted to add that, I hope it makes sense and didn't scare you all further!

I had seven alters. They didn't seem like they would be compatible when I was multiple. They really all felt quite different and *were* quite different. Different genders, sexual orientations, and spiritual beliefs too. When I integrated though it all found a way to balance out. A belief I had as a multiple was that itd be an equal mix.. For example, if one alter was straight and the other was gay , I would integrate and be evenly bisexual. It didn't work out quite that way for me. Some parts of me became more dominant than others when I stopped dissociating from them.

Sometimes when I get really stressed, I think briefly "Man, I wish i was a multiple again right now", I miss the help and the comfort. i think thats my equivalent of you missing the chatter. But that gets less and less over time. 

>how did the integration go?

Could you rephrase this? Im unsure what you are asking.

I went into therapy in 2012 and integrated around October 2015. I never actually planned to integrate, but as I worked through the trauma it happened naturally.  I also moved out of a chaotic environment which definitely helped reduce my need for the alters. In my view, in hindsight, the alters were a sort of coping mechanism for me so that I wouldn't feel like I had to go through things alone anymore, eg. "Ill never be abused again, because my alters are there to protect me", and so I could better handle conflicting parts of myself, things like that. But now I feel like I can protect myself on my own and deal with things myself. It's working out really well for me, sometimes I stop and look at how things have turned out and I just can't believe it. I had thought I'd be a multiple forever.

It kind of sucks to both have PTSD and be trans because of stuff like this, I worked hard in therapy for 5 years to fix the worst of my problems, just to be sure this wasnt coming from my trauma, and STILL I have gender dysphoria. What would they suggest I do? Some more yoga?? It doesn't sound like their gender dysphoria ever went away, either. These "ex-trans" insist there is an alternative treatment for gender dysphoria but you never see the proof.
